title: Identifier Case Converter
instructions:
Implement the class `IdentifierConverter` in `identifiers.py` with four instance methods.
It has no constructor arguments or stored configuration. Inputs to name methods are strings.

`split(name: str) -> list[str]` validates and splits an identifier into lowercase tokens.
Valid names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(?:_[A-Za-z0-9]+)*` using ASCII characters only.
Invalid names (including empty strings, leading/trailing/doubled underscores, punctuation,
spaces or non-ASCII letters) raise `ValueError`. Underscores separate chunks. Within each
chunk, split lowercase-to-uppercase boundaries, the last capital of an acronym when it
starts a lowercase word, and every letter/digit boundary. Consecutive digits stay together.
Examples: `HTTPServer2_ID` -> `['http', 'server', '2', 'id']`, `a12B` -> `['a', '12', 'b']`,
`XML` -> `['xml']`, `version_2_value` -> `['version', '2', 'value']`.

- `to_snake(name: str) -> str`: join split tokens with underscores.
- `to_camel(name: str, upper: bool = False) -> str`: join tokens with each word capitalized
  (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase). When upper is False, leave the first token
  lowercase. Digit tokens remain unchanged.
- `convert(name: str, style: str) -> str`: dispatch to snake, lower camel, or upper camel
  for exact styles `'snake'`, `'camel'`, `'pascal'`. Any other style raises `ValueError`.
All three conversion methods apply the same input validation as split.

## Files
- `identifiers.py`
